short_title: Rare earth elements in the waste (2021)
title: Rare earth elements characterization associated to the phosphate fertilizer plants of Gabes (Tunisia, Central Mediterranean Sea): Geochemical properties and behavior, related economic losses, and potential hazards
summary: Measured 16 rare earth elements in phosphate rock, phosphogypsum and foam. The foam had the most. Estimates that up to 1,523.67 tonnes of these elements reach the sea each year, a wasted resource worth about 58 million US dollars a year.

findings.headline: Up to 1,523.67 tonnes of rare earth metals reach the sea each year
findings.summary: This is the estimated yearly amount of rare earth elements going from the fertiliser factories into the sea. The authors value this loss at about 58 million US dollars a year.
findings.headline_original: Up to 1,523.67 tonnes of rare earths reach the sea each year
findings.summary_original: Estimated annual flow of rare earth elements from the fertilizer factories to the marine environment; related economic loss estimated at about 58 million US dollars per year.
